crust.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for Earth's crust, via PubChem ('2.2×10¹ milligrams per kilogram').

solar.note: Proto-solar (4.567 Ga ago) elemental mass fraction, column 'Elemental Mass Fractions' of ESM Table A13; the table gives no uncertainty (relative sigma of N(E) in Table 6 applies).

solarLogEps.note: A(E) = log10(N_E/N_H) + 12, 'Solar System Present' log (E/H)+12; basis: meteoritic (CI-chondrite) value; unc = 1 sigma in dex as printed.

body.note: Our table from ICRP Publication 23 has no amount for this element in the reference body (tools/curated/abundance.toml lists what was left out and why).

temperature.note: The COD entry does not state the temperature of the measurement.

crystal.note: Sample 99.6 % pure (CIF). Temperature not stated in CIF.

tonnesPerYear.note: World global production, scandium oxide equivalent, 2025 (USGS: 80 metric tons).

unitValue.note: Price, global, dollars per kilogram, range of average values: Scandium oxide, powder, 99.99% purity, 5- to 100-kilogram lot size [Scandium], 2025; per kg of the material named, as USGS gives it.

origin.note: Read off Fig. 39 at the dotted 'age of the Sun' line (t = 9.2 Gyr after the Big Bang, 4.6 Gyr ago): pixel fractions of the stacked areas (massive_stars 0.959, white_dwarfs 0.041); quantised to 0.05. Stack height 14 px. LOW PRECISION: the model abundance is small on this box's scale, so 1 px = 0.07 of the total. Paper: 'For the elements from Ne to Ge, the newly synthesized amounts are very small for AGB stars, and the small green areas are mostly for mass loss.' Paper: 'K, Sc, V and Ti are known to be under-produced at all metallicity ranges in theoretical models with respect to the observations' and 'The under-production of the elements around Ti is a long-standing problem.'

splitting.note: 3d4s2 2D3/2 ground level. Laser-rf double resonance on an atomic beam with resonance-ionisation detection (de Groote et al. 2022, arXiv:2005.00414 Table 2). These are the values fitted directly to the measured intervals, before second-order correction, so they reproduce the observed splitting. Childs (1971) gives B = -26.346(4) MHz, which differs by about 1.7 sigma. Splitting = width of the ground-level hyperfine manifold (F = 2 to 5), from A and B.

biology.note: Not known to be essential for plants or for humans.

history.nameOrigin: From Scandia, the Latin name for Scandinavia, where its minerals were found.
history.note: Cleve showed the same year that it was Mendeleev's predicted eka-boron. Los Alamos gives 1878. The 1937 metal preparation: Z. anorg. allg. Chem. 231, 54 (doi:10.1002/zaac.19372310107).

prose.text: Scandium is a light, silvery transition metal, named after Scandinavia, where its minerals were found; small additions of it strengthen the aluminium alloys used in some aircraft parts and sports equipment. Its existence was foreseen: Mendeleev left a gap in his table for an element he called eka-boron and predicted its properties, and scandium, discovered in 1879, filled that gap closely. Scandium is the first element to place an electron in a 3d orbital, giving [Ar] 3d¹ 4s² and the ground term ²D₃/₂, yet in compounds it almost always gives away all three outer electrons; with no d electrons left, its compounds are usually colourless.
